title: Share the GPU's encoder sessions between 1080p and 4K jobs

blocks.text: The transcoding service shares one GPU between jobs. The GPU runs five hardware encoder sessions at once: a 1080p job needs one, and a 4K job needs four. Three problems are in the backlog. On the night two 4K jobs arrived together, both stalled until someone restarted the service. The "try now, else requeue" path sometimes leaves the GPU with fewer free sessions than its gauge should show. And on busy days a 4K job can sit for an hour while 1080p jobs that arrived after it keep getting sessions.

Finish the three `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/EncoderSessions.java`: `newSessions(...)`, `reserve(...)` and `tryReserve(...)`. When you're done, a job gets all the sessions it asked for or none of them, whether it waits, is refused, or is cancelled while waiting; and a waiting 4K job is not passed by 1080p jobs that arrive after it. About three lines in total.
The tests run jobs on real threads and cancel them through their `Future`, which interrupts them.

cases.says: a job that can have its sessions now gets them, and sessions given back can be reserved again
a job that needs more sessions than are free waits, and gets them once enough are given back
a job waiting for several sessions holds none of them while it waits
a job that cannot have all its sessions now is refused and takes none of them
a job cancelled while it waits for sessions stops waiting at once and holds none
a 1-session job that arrives while a larger job waits does not take a session ahead of it

origin.section: acquire(n) Takes All n Permits at Once or None

concepts: acquire(n) and tryAcquire(n) take all n permits together or none, including when interrupted, so a waiting job never holds part of what another needs.
On a non-fair semaphore a waiting acquire(n) can be overtaken by smaller requests; a fair one queues them behind it.
